items.issues: Clement's mockery → hesitant care with the iron is clear; distractors each misattribute the end state (grief/anger/relief). Clean medium.
Triumph (sold out, haggling, laughter) → heaviness (kettle forgotten twice). C's 'relief' is tempting only on the surface; A reverses the order.
'I had, I believe, a closing argument' signals self-mocking amusement; D (wistful longing) is the only near miss and lacks support.
Requires joining cooperative-knot practice with the sailor's hitch on the trusted gate; A is a plot summary, B contradicts, D moralizes. Solid medium, not hard.
Unpaid early hours + untouched ledger + bread left 'without having to thank me' all point to A; B/C impose motives the text undercuts.
The priest states the symbol's meaning almost outright ('only to let it come back'), so the item reads easy; C is the only partly tempting wrong answer.
Milena finishing the corner in the same strokes and the mother taking the dustpan make C the fit; B is tempting but the mother does talk about the wedding while sweeping.
'not yet been paid to color', shadow 'as large as he liked', form sliding to floor support D; A inverts (fire vs blank), B is literal, C is a decent misread.
Neighbors' remark + turning her back on it make C clear; A invents husband's gardening, D overreads Theo. Fine medium.
Cake anecdote (month of silence) nails 'fence' as a barrier against thanks; 'built himself' rules out C. Leans easy-medium.
Dread (rehearsed refusals, stiffening) → relief (list of favors, feet in water) is unmistakable; distractors are coherent but easily eliminated.
'Not again' / 'repeatedly' twice → 'I did not know what you were listening for' / open door; only D matches both ends. Easy.
Sentence recasts a year of resented silence as attention; B (explains the rule's origin) is the plausible trap but the sentence interprets, not explains.

Pausing and restarting the sentence over 'never once mentioned the ball' reads as moved appreciation; D (regret at his childhood misjudgment) is partly defensible since the text contrasts his age-eleven verdict, but B is the better overall fit.

Most of the passage is companionable banter (tower debate, grant joke) with unease surfacing only in the mid-word stop and the slow sixth cup, favoring D; but 'laughed louder than the joke deserved' makes C's 'humor masks worry' genuinely arguable. Weight judgment between C and D carries real multi-answer risk.
